If we assume that the two populations have the same variance, we can use both samples to estimate that common variance.

The **pooled variance** is

$$\large
s_p^2
=
\frac{
(n_1-1)s_1^2+(n_2-1)s_2^2
}{
n_1+n_2-2
}.
$$

The pooled standard deviation is therefore

$$\large
s_p=\sqrt{s_p^2}.
$$

This is essentially a **weighted average of the two sample variances**, with larger samples contributing more information.

> Pooling makes sense only because we are assuming that both sample variances are estimating the **same population variance** $\sigma^2$.
